description: Buffer overflow gated behind a magic UART byte (gate == 0xA5) -- the hard problem the generic fixed-pattern concrete driver ('A'-filled payload) cannot solve on its own. Requires the angr-based symbolic path-solve fallback (dvl.oracle_pathsolve) to synthesize an input satisfying the gate before the generic driver's Inconclusive verdict would otherwise be final.

cases.reason: cmd[8] is written with no bound check on the loop index i, but only after gate == 0xA5. The generic 'A'-filled (0x41) payload never satisfies the gate, so the concrete driver alone reports Inconclusive; the angr path-solve fallback must synthesize a first byte of 0xA5 (plus enough following bytes) to actually drive execution into the vulnerable loop and trigger the overflow.

Same magic-byte gate (still requires the path-solve fallback to reach at all), but the write index is bounds-checked (i <= 7) before every write. No OOB write occurs for any sequence of injected bytes.
